description: Specific statistical methods must be named to classify the system as a model. Vague terms are insufficient.
Specific AI/ML techniques must be named to classify the system as a model. General terms without specifics are not acceptable.
The system must explicitly generate predictions about future events or behaviors to be classified as a model. Descriptive reporting alone is not sufficient.
Specific optimization methods must be named to classify the system as a model. General optimization terms without methodology details are insufficient.
Parameter estimation methods must be clearly described to classify the system as a model. Fixed parameters or vague descriptions are not acceptable.
Escalate when the system is likely a model but lacks uncertainty documentation.
Escalate when the system is likely a model but lacks formal validation documentation.
Escalate when critical methodology details are missing after two clarification rounds.
Generate clarification questions when ambiguous statistical methods are mentioned without specifics.
Generate clarification questions when adaptive elements are mentioned without specific algorithms.
Generate clarification questions when parameter estimation is mentioned without details.
Generate clarification questions when model-like behavior is denied despite evidence of such behavior.
Generate clarification questions when validation documentation is missing or insufficient.
Generate clarification questions when uncertainty documentation is missing despite model-like behavior.
